packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET 11 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: No proposed identification of the work or author was revealed to me. The images carry modern pencil labels "Stams, STA, Frg. 123r" (image-001/003/004) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 123v" (image-005/007/008), a red-framed paper label "C. 6"? (image-004), and a modern pencil note on face B "Einband zu ... II/[?] 34 (anno 1586?)" (image-006/007; partly read, digits uncertain). These are shelfmark/provenance notes, not identifications of the text, and I have not used them. Nothing done beyond the rules. Images opened: image-001 to image-008 (image-009 does not exist). All loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- A narrow horizontal parchment strip (binding waste), two faces, each an overview + 3 tiles:
  Face A (label 123r): image-001 overview (photographed with the ruler upside down, text upright); image-002 = left part; image-003 = middle; image-004 = right part.
  Face B (label 123v): image-005 overview; image-006 = left part; image-007 = middle; image-008 = right part.
- Only 5-7 text lines survive per block; below them is blank parchment (apparently lower margin), so these look like the last lines of columns, but the crop does not prove that. Folds/creases and stitching slits run vertically; tabs at the ends are taped.
- Face A: three blocks: (i) a narrow block at far left showing only line-ends (image-002), (ii) a full middle column, (iii) a right column. A further fragmentary line on the left taped tab ("[..]anistro i"). Single hand, brown-black ink, Gothic book hand with heavy abbreviation. No rubrics on face A.
- Face B: left column with a large red/orange two-line initial "A" and red rubric text at line-end (two rubric lines, see 006.04-05); middle column in paler, browner ink (same or similar hand, abraded); narrow right block of line-starts (image-008), partly under tape. Rubric includes "Sermo" (tentative interpretation: homiletic text, a sermon heading). Also a doxology-type closing line before the initial (006.03).
- No interlinear or marginal glosses seen; no lemma/commentary structure.

CONVENTIONS: line numbers from the top of each image (first text line = 1). ( ) = expansion; ? = uncertain; [..] / [illegible] = unread. Overlaps noted, not double-counted.

========================================
FACE A (123r)
Block (i), far left, line-ends only (image-002)

Right block, line-starts only (image-008; partly under clear tape)

008.05  electione app[..]
008.06  legem? mu[..]
008.07  [..] tanta? [..]mor[..]
(image-008 lines 1-7 at left also repeat the ends of 007.01-07; overlap only.)

========================================
SELECTED / UNREAD
- Read: every visible text line on both faces (strip holds only ~6-7 lines per block). Most secure: face B left column 006.03-006.07 (closing formula, initial A + rubric, quoted line) and face A middle/right columns 003.01-003.04, 004.01-004.04.
- Weak: face A 003.05 and 004.05-07; face B middle column (pale ink) and right block (line-starts under tape); the rubric word before "andue".
- Unread: anything above the top edge of the strip (cut off) and the left block on face A beyond its line-ends.

LIMITATIONS
- Strip is cut at top and sides; column order across the folds is assumed left-to-right as photographed. Which face is recto is not assumed.
- Abbreviation expansions marked ? are tentative; I have not filled gaps from expected sense.
- Suggested extra imaging: raking-light or UV of face A lower lines (003.05, 004.05-07) and of face B middle column; a view of the right-hand block on face B with the tape lifted or from an angle.
